Class WindowHandle

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.window.WindowHandle
Direct Known Subclasses:
ElementHandle, PanelHandle, SlotHandle
public abstract sealed class WindowHandle extends Object permits SlotHandle, ElementHandle, PanelHandle
The base of THE ONE WINDOW's typed handle family — an immutable value addressing one thing by its Address, never by a held live reference (the menu and every Slot are recreated each reopen, so a held reference would dangle). Carries only the address; equals/hashCode are over it, so two handles naming the same thing are interchangeable and safe as map keys.

Two-layer surface (architecture Part 2 §2)

  • Generic substrate (here, every kind): set(BehaviorKey, Decl)/behavior(BehaviorKey) — the engine is the truth. Any behavior, including ones added later, with zero new handle code.
  • Named sugar (the typed subclasses): SlotHandle.onInsert(...), PanelHandle.opacity(...) — thin, discoverable wrappers over the substrate, restricted per kind so a slot verb is unreachable on a panel handle (compile-checked).

The handle never returns the raw backing (no getSlot()), per the Law of Demeter — reads go through behavior(BehaviorKey), which resolves the engine cascade and is always non-null. Writes route to WindowEngine.set(Address, BehaviorKey, Decl) (a SERVER-tier key with MKC absent is a safe no-op via the NoServerTier port).

Sealed to the three kinds that exist; new kinds extend the family additively (KindTag is FROZEN-OPEN). A handle is a value — held by the consumer, resolved per call (late binding), so one consumer line addresses "this thing" across reopen, across sides, and across the vanilla/created divide.
